summary: Blueprint for global Galois deformation rings, within the RS-08 boundaries (accepted). Checkpoints 1–2 plan the retained parts of R04.1 and R04.2: the lifting (framed) functor, module deformations and their identification with lifts up to strict conjugation, strict versus full conjugacy, restriction to subgroups and the invariance of framed local restrictions, fixed-determinant variants, change of coefficients, the separate determinant (pseudorepresentation) deformation functor with its comparison, and tangent spaces (R04.1); Mazur's condition Φ_p and its verification for G_{F,S} and G_K, the universal lifting ring and continuous universal lift, the universal deformation ring for Schur residual representations, the framed-unframed comparison with n² − 1 variables, Carayol's theorem, fixed-determinant rings with the change-of-determinant decomposition for p ∤ n, and change of residue field (R04.2). Coefficient categories and Schlessinger's criterion are imported from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.2, global finiteness from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3, determinants from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0. Checkpoint 2 adds R04.3: local deformation problems and their ideals, global deformation data with T-framings and representability, the map from local rings, the relative tangent space as an adjoint Selmer group, the presentation R^loc[[x₁..x_g]]/J with r(J) bounded by the dual Selmer group, and the dimension lower bound (Gee §3.16–3.24, KW II §4.1). Checkpoint 3 adds R04.4 (12 nodes): restriction to a finite extension with its finiteness and a finite non-flat example, closed immersions from enlarging S, twisting isomorphisms and change of determinant, KW II's diagonalizable groups, free-action quotients and truncated actions, the twisting action with its dyadic freeness and stabilisers, the rings with determinant fixed only on S and the determinant torsor, and inertia-rigid deformation rings (KW II §§2.4–2.7, 4.1, 5.1–5.2, 9, 10.1; Gee 3.25–3.26; BLGGT 1.2.3). It also records how KW II Corollary 4.7 uses the R04.3 dimension bound, and records the published numbering of KW II from the authors' final version.

nodes.title: The lifting (framed deformation) functor
nodes.statement: Setting: G is a profinite group, 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p (or W(𝔽)) with residue field 𝔽 finite of characteristic p, n ≥ 1, and ρ̄ : G → GL_n(𝔽) is continuous. Art_𝒪 is the category of Artinian local 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 and C_𝒪 that of complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 (both imported from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1). Γ̂_n(A) := ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(𝔽)). The lifting functor Lift_ρ̄ : Art_𝒪 → Set sends A to the set of continuous homomorphisms ρ : G → GL_n(A) (A discrete) with ρ mod m_A = ρ̄; a morphism f : A → B acts by ρ ↦ GL_n(f)∘ρ. On C_𝒪 it is extended by continuity: Lift_ρ̄(A) is the set of continuous lifts for the m_A-adic topology, and equals lim_k Lift_ρ̄(A/m_A^k).
hypotheses: Pro-representability is not part of the definition (RS-08): Lift_ρ̄ is a plain functor; its representability is universal-lifting-ring.
Continuity: for A Artinian, GL_n(A) is finite and discrete, so ρ is continuous iff it factors through an open normal subgroup.
proofSteps: Functoriality: GL_n(f) is a continuous group homomorphism and preserves the reduction to 𝔽 because f is a local 𝒪-algebra map inducing the identity on 𝔽.
The limit description on C_𝒪: a homomorphism into GL_n(A) = lim GL_n(A/m_A^k) is continuous iff each reduction is, since A is m_A-adically complete and separated.
acceptance: For n = 1 and ρ̄ = 1, Lift(A) = Hom_cont(G, 1 + m_A), which for G = ℤ_p is 1 + m_A.
For A = 𝔽, Lift_ρ̄(𝔽) = {ρ̄}.
For G finite of order prime to p every lift is conjugate to the Teichmüller lift (H¹ = 0), but Lift(A) is not a single point in general.

nodes.title: Deformations as modules with a residual identification
nodes.statement: Setting: G is a profinite group, 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p (or W(𝔽)) with residue field 𝔽 finite of characteristic p, n ≥ 1, and ρ̄ : G → GL_n(𝔽) is continuous. Art_𝒪 is the category of Artinian local 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 and C_𝒪 that of complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 (both imported from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1). Γ̂_n(A) := ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(𝔽)). Fix V̄ = 𝔽^n with G acting by ρ̄ and its standard basis β. A deformation of V̄ to A ∈ Art_𝒪 is a pair (V_A, ι) with V_A a finite free A-module with a continuous A-linear G-action and ι : V_A ⊗_A 𝔽 ≅ V̄ a G-equivariant isomorphism; a framed deformation adds an A-basis β_A of V_A lifting β through ι. Isomorphisms are G-equivariant A-linear isomorphisms compatible with ι (and with the bases). Def^mod_ρ̄(A) and Def^{mod,□}_ρ̄(A) are the sets of isomorphism classes.
hypotheses: Bases lifting β exist for every (V_A, ι) because V_A is free and V_A → V_A ⊗ 𝔽 is surjective (Nakayama).
proofSteps: Base change along f : A → B sends (V_A, ι) to (V_A ⊗_A B, ι ⊗ 𝔽), compatibly with bases; isomorphisms go to isomorphisms.
acceptance: Def^{mod,□}_ρ̄(𝔽) and Def^mod_ρ̄(𝔽) are singletons.
For ρ̄ = 1 (n = 1) Def^mod(A) = Hom_cont(G, 1 + m_A), since automorphisms of rank-one modules are scalars and act trivially.
An isomorphism of deformations is required to be compatible with ι; dropping this gives a different (coarser) functor.

nodes.title: Deformations up to strict equivalence
nodes.statement: Setting: G is a profinite group, 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p (or W(𝔽)) with residue field 𝔽 finite of characteristic p, n ≥ 1, and ρ̄ : G → GL_n(𝔽) is continuous. Art_𝒪 is the category of Artinian local 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 and C_𝒪 that of complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 (both imported from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1). Γ̂_n(A) := ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(𝔽)). The deformation functor Def_ρ̄ : Art_𝒪 → Set is A ↦ Lift_ρ̄(A)/Γ̂_n(A), lifts up to conjugation by Γ̂_n(A) = ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(𝔽)) (strict equivalence). It is defined for every ρ̄; its representability needs End_{𝔽[G]}(ρ̄) = 𝔽 (universal-deformation-ring).
hypotheses: Strict equivalence, not GL_n(A)-conjugacy: the two agree when ρ̄ is Schur (strict-vs-full-conjugacy) but not in general.
proofSteps: Γ̂_n(A) is a normal subgroup of GL_n(A) and conjugation preserves the reduction ρ̄ (the conjugating matrix reduces to 1), so the quotient is well defined.
Functoriality: GL_n(f) maps Γ̂_n(A) into Γ̂_n(B) and is equivariant.
acceptance: Def_ρ̄(𝔽) is a singleton.
For n = 1, Def = Lift (Γ̂_1 is central).
Def_ρ̄(𝔽[ε]) ≅ H¹(G, ad ρ̄) (tangent-spaces).

nodes.title: Module deformations are lifts up to strict conjugation
nodes.statement: Choosing bases lifting β gives natural bijections Lift_ρ̄(A) ≅ Def^{mod,□}_ρ̄(A) and Lift_ρ̄(A)/Γ̂_n(A) ≅ Def^mod_ρ̄(A), compatible with base change: the equivalence relation on lifts that corresponds to isomorphism of module deformations is exactly conjugation by Γ̂_n(A).
hypotheses: A ∈ Art_𝒪; the same holds on C_𝒪 with continuity for the m_A-adic topology.
proofSteps: To (V_A, ι, β_A) attach the matrix of the G-action in β_A: a continuous lift of ρ̄ because β_A reduces to β.
Two bases of V_A lifting β differ by a matrix in Γ̂_n(A), and changing the basis conjugates the matrix by it.

An isomorphism (V_A, ι) ≅ (V′_A, ι′) compatible with ι sends bases lifting β to bases lifting β, so isomorphic deformations give strictly equivalent lifts, and conversely a conjugating matrix in Γ̂_n(A) defines such an isomorphism.
Every (V_A, ι) has a basis lifting β (module-deformation-functor), so the maps are surjective.
acceptance: For A = 𝔽[ε] this recovers Ext¹_G(V̄, V̄) ≅ H¹(G, ad ρ̄) (Kisin Lemma 1.3.1).
The bijection commutes with Lift.map and ModDef.baseChange.
Replacing Γ̂_n(A) by GL_n(A) gives isomorphism classes of G-modules forgetting ι, which differ for non-Schur ρ̄.

sources.match: The statement; the proof steps spell out the basis-change argument.

nodes.title: Strict and full conjugacy agree for Schur residual representations
nodes.statement: If End_{𝔽[G]}(ρ̄) = 𝔽 (ρ̄ is Schur; e.g. ρ̄ absolutely irreducible), then two lifts ρ, ρ′ ∈ Lift_ρ̄(A) that are conjugate by some a ∈ GL_n(A) are conjugate by some b ∈ Γ̂_n(A). Without the Schur hypothesis this fails.
hypotheses: End_{𝔽[G]}(ρ̄) = 𝔽 (Schur's lemma gives this for absolutely irreducible ρ̄).
proofSteps: Reducing aρa^{-1} = ρ′ modulo m_A shows that ā ∈ GL_n(𝔽) commutes with ρ̄, so ā = c ∈ 𝔽^× by the Schur hypothesis.
Let c̃ ∈ 𝒪^× lift c (e.g. its Teichmüller lift) and b := c̃^{-1}a; then b ∈ Γ̂_n(A) and bρb^{-1} = aρa^{-1} = ρ′ because scalars are central.
acceptance: For ρ̄ absolutely irreducible over a finite field the hypothesis holds.

Counterexample without Schur: ρ̄ = 1 ⊕ 1, A = 𝔽[ε], ρ = diag(1 + εx, 1), ρ′ = diag(1, 1 + εx) with x : G → 𝔽 a nonzero continuous homomorphism: conjugate by the swap matrix, but Γ̂₂(𝔽[ε]) acts trivially on lifts of the scalar ρ̄.
This is the equivalence stated parenthetically in Gee Definition 3.4.

sources.match: The equivalence under the Schur hypothesis of Definition 3.4; the proof is the two proof steps.

nodes.title: Restriction of lifts and deformations is well defined
nodes.statement: Let ι : H → G be a continuous homomorphism of profinite groups (e.g. a decomposition group G_v → G_{F,S}). Composition gives a natural transformation Lift_ρ̄ → Lift_{ρ̄∘ι} which is Γ̂_n-equivariant, hence induces Def_ρ̄ → Def_{ρ̄∘ι}. Moreover, on pairs (ρ, α) with ρ ∈ Lift_ρ̄(A) and α ∈ Γ̂_n(A), modulo (ρ, α) ∼ (βρβ^{-1}, βα) for β ∈ Γ̂_n(A), the local lift α^{-1}(ρ∘ι)α ∈ Lift_{ρ̄∘ι}(A) depends only on the class.
hypotheses: The last statement is what makes the framed local restriction of a T-framed global deformation (R04.3, G8) well defined.
proofSteps: Composition with a continuous homomorphism preserves continuity and the reduction to ρ̄∘ι.
(βρβ^{-1})∘ι = β(ρ∘ι)β^{-1}, so strict classes go to strict classes.
acceptance: Restriction to an open subgroup of an absolutely irreducible ρ̄ need not be Schur, so Def_ρ̄ → Def_{ρ̄|H} can land in a non-representable functor.
For ι the identity the transformation is the identity.
The framed restriction is invariant: replacing (ρ, α) by (βρβ^{-1}, βα) gives the same local lift.

sources.match: The invariance of the framed local restriction.

nodes.title: Lifts and deformations with fixed determinant
nodes.statement: Let χ : G → 𝒪^× be continuous with χ mod λ = det ρ̄. Lift_{ρ̄,χ}(A) := {ρ ∈ Lift_ρ̄(A) : det ρ = χ_A}, χ_A the composite G → 𝒪^× → A^×; it is stable under Γ̂_n(A), and Def_{ρ̄,χ} := Lift_{ρ̄,χ}/Γ̂_n. These are subfunctors of Lift_ρ̄ and Def_ρ̄.
hypotheses: The determinant is not fixed in the variable-determinant problems of G8; this is the separate fixed-determinant variant.
proofSteps: det(aρa^{-1}) = det ρ, and det commutes with GL_n(f), so the conditions are functorial and conjugation-stable.
acceptance: For n = 1, Lift_{ρ̄,χ}(A) = {χ_A}.
If p ∤ n, the tangent space of Lift_{ρ̄,χ} is Z¹(G, ad⁰ρ̄), ad⁰ the trace-zero matrices (Gee Exercise 3.19).
If p | n, ad⁰ρ̄ need not be a direct summand of ad ρ̄, and the tangent space must be computed with ad⁰ itself.

nodes.title: Change of coefficient ring and residue field
nodes.statement: Let 𝒪 → 𝒪′ be a local homomorphism of such coefficient rings, finite, with residue extension 𝔽 ⊆ 𝔽′, and ρ̄′ := ρ̄ ⊗_𝔽 𝔽′. Restriction along 𝒪 → 𝒪′ identifies Lift^{𝒪′}_{ρ̄′}(A′) with the set of lifts of ρ̄ to A′ in the sense of local 𝒪-algebras whose residue map 𝔽 → 𝔽′ is the given inclusion, naturally in A′ ∈ Art_{𝒪′}; the same holds for Def, for fixed determinant, and for Schur ρ̄ (End_{𝔽′[G]}(ρ̄′) = End_{𝔽[G]}(ρ̄) ⊗ 𝔽′ = 𝔽′).
hypotheses: The categories Art_{𝒪′} and the residue-field-extension API come from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1.
proofSteps: A lift of ρ̄′ to A′ is a continuous homomorphism G → GL_n(A′) reducing to ρ̄ ⊗ 𝔽′; this is intrinsic to A′ and ρ̄.
Strict conjugation and determinants are compatible with the change of rings.
Schur is preserved: End_{𝔽′[G]}(ρ̄ ⊗ 𝔽′) = End_{𝔽[G]}(ρ̄) ⊗_𝔽 𝔽′ because taking G-invariants of ad ρ̄ commutes with the field extension.
acceptance: For ρ̄ a character and 𝔽 = 𝔽′, changing 𝒪 to a ramified extension 𝒪′ changes the representing ring by ⊗̂_𝒪 𝒪′.
Absolute irreducibility and Schur are preserved by 𝔽 → 𝔽′.
Irreducibility (not absolute) is not preserved: an irreducible ρ̄ over 𝔽 can split over 𝔽′.

nodes.title: Deformations of a residual determinant
nodes.statement: Let D̄ := det ∘ ρ̄ : 𝔽[G] → 𝔽, a continuous determinant of dimension n in Chenevier's sense (a multiplicative polynomial law homogeneous of degree n; the foundations are imported from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0). Def_{D̄}(A) is the set of continuous determinants D : A[G] → A of dimension n with D ⊗_A 𝔽 = D̄, for A ∈ Art_𝒪 (and by continuity for A ∈ C_𝒪). It is a separate functor: it is not assumed equivalent to Def_ρ̄ (determinant-comparison).
hypotheses: Continuity of a determinant: its characteristic-polynomial coefficients g ↦ Λ_i(g) are continuous (Chenevier §2.30).
proofSteps: Functoriality: base change of polynomial laws along local 𝒪-algebra maps preserves dimension, multiplicativity and continuity.
acceptance: For n = 1, a determinant is a character and Def_{D̄} = Lift_{χ̄} = Def_{χ̄}.
For ρ̄ = χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ reducible, Def_{D̄} depends only on {χ₁, χ₂} and not on an extension class.

nodes.title: Representation deformations versus determinant deformations
nodes.statement: ρ ↦ det ∘ ρ (the determinant of the A-linear extension A[G] → M_n(A)) induces a natural transformation Def_ρ̄ → Def_{det∘ρ̄}. If ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible it is an isomorphism of functors. In general it is not injective.
hypotheses: The isomorphism uses Chenevier's Theorem 2.22 (a determinant over a henselian local ring with split absolutely irreducible residue is det∘ρ for a unique-up-to-conjugation ρ) together with Carayol's lemma.
proofSteps: Well defined: det(aρa^{-1}) = det ρ as polynomial laws.

Surjectivity for absolutely irreducible ρ̄: for A Artinian (hence henselian), a determinant D lifting det∘ρ̄ with split absolutely irreducible residue is det∘ρ_D for some representation ρ_D : A[G] → M_n(A) (Chenevier Theorem 2.22(i)); ρ_D reduces to a conjugate of ρ̄, and conjugating gives a lift.
Injectivity for absolutely irreducible ρ̄: equal determinants give equal traces, and Carayol's lemma (carayol-trace-theorem) gives strict conjugacy.

Non-injectivity in general: for ρ̄ a non-split extension of χ₂ by χ₁ with dim Ext¹(χ₂, χ₁) > 1 there are non-isomorphic deformations with the same traces (Kisin Exercise 3), hence the same determinant.
acceptance: For n = 1 the transformation is the identity.
For ρ̄ absolutely irreducible, the universal rings agree: R_ρ̄ ≅ the determinant deformation ring.
For ρ̄ = 1 ⊕ 1 the transformation forgets the extension data and is not injective on 𝔽[ε]-points.

nodes.title: Tangent spaces of the lifting and deformation functors
nodes.statement: Let 𝔽[ε] = 𝔽[X]/(X²) and ad ρ̄ = M_n(𝔽) with G acting by conjugation through ρ̄. Then φ ↦ (1 + εφ)ρ̄ is a bijection Z¹(G, ad ρ̄) ≅ Lift_ρ̄(𝔽[ε]) (continuous cocycles), inducing H¹(G, ad ρ̄) ≅ Def_ρ̄(𝔽[ε]); the fibres of Lift_ρ̄(𝔽[ε]) → Def_ρ̄(𝔽[ε]) are torsors under ad ρ̄/(ad ρ̄)^G. Hence, when these are finite, dim_𝔽 Lift_ρ̄(𝔽[ε]) = dim H¹(G, ad ρ̄) + n² − dim H⁰(G, ad ρ̄). With fixed determinant (p ∤ n), ad is replaced by ad⁰.
hypotheses: G acts on ad ρ̄ by g·X = ρ̄(g)Xρ̄(g)^{-1}; ad ρ̄ is a finite discrete G-module, so continuous cochains are locally constant.
The vector space structures come from the fibre-product structure of Art_𝒪 (R03.1).
proofSteps: (1 + εφ(gh))ρ̄(gh) = (1 + εφ(g))ρ̄(g)(1 + εφ(h))ρ̄(h) ⟺ φ(gh) = φ(g) + g·φ(h), the cocycle identity.
Conjugating by 1 + εB ∈ Γ̂_n(𝔽[ε]) changes φ by the coboundary g ↦ B − g·B.
The stabiliser of a lift under Γ̂_n(𝔽[ε]) ≅ ad ρ̄ is (ad ρ̄)^G, so fibres are torsors under ad ρ̄/(ad ρ̄)^G; the dimension formula follows from 0 → (ad ρ̄)^G → ad ρ̄ → Z¹ → H¹ → 0.
acceptance: n = 1, ρ̄ = 1, G = G_{ℚ,{p}}: Lift(𝔽[ε]) = Hom(G, 𝔽) = 𝔽 for p odd (the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension).
ρ̄ absolutely irreducible: dim Lift(𝔽[ε]) = dim H¹(G, ad ρ̄) + n² − 1.
The torsor statement fails for Γ̂_n replaced by GL_n: the fibres are then quotients by a larger group.

nodes.title: Mazur's finiteness condition Φ_p
nodes.statement: A profinite group G satisfies Φ_p if for every open subgroup Δ ≤ G the group Hom_cont(Δ, 𝔽_p) is finite; equivalently, the maximal pro-p quotient of every open subgroup is topologically finitely generated.
hypotheses: The condition quantifies over all open subgroups; finiteness of Hom(G, 𝔽_p) alone is weaker (sourceIssues E1).
proofSteps: Equivalence: Hom_cont(Δ, 𝔽_p) is the dual of the Frattini quotient Δ^{(p)}/Φ(Δ^{(p)}) of the maximal pro-p quotient, which is finite iff Δ^{(p)} is topologically finitely generated (Burnside basis theorem for pro-p groups).
acceptance: Topologically finitely generated profinite groups satisfy Φ_p.
G_K for K/ℚ_ℓ finite satisfies Φ_p (K^×/K^{×p} is finite); G_{F,S} does too (phi-p-global).
Non-example: G = (∏_ℕ ℤ/p) ⋊ ℤ/2 (p odd, ℤ/2 acting by inversion) has Hom(G, 𝔽_p) = 0 but its index-2 subgroup has infinite Hom to 𝔽_p.

nodes.title: Global and local Galois groups satisfy Φ_p
nodes.statement: For a number field F and a finite set S of places, G_{F,S} = Gal(F_S/F) satisfies Φ_p; for a finite extension K/ℚ_ℓ (ℓ possibly = p), G_K satisfies Φ_p.
hypotheses: F_S is the maximal extension of F unramified outside S and the infinite places.
proofSteps: Every open subgroup of G_{F,S} is G_{F′,S′} for a finite extension F′/F inside F_S and S′ the places above S.

Hom_cont(G_{F′,S′}, 𝔽_p) classifies cyclic degree-p extensions of F′ unramified outside S′, of bounded discriminant; they are finitely many (Hermite–Minkowski, or class field theory via the finiteness of the ray class group modulo p-power conductor at S′): this finiteness is imported from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3.
Locally, Hom(G_K, 𝔽_p) = Hom(K^×/K^{×p}, 𝔽_p) by local class field theory, and K^×/K^{×p} is finite; open subgroups are G_{K′} for finite K′/K.
acceptance: G_{ℚ,{p,∞}} satisfies Φ_p although it is not known to be topologically finitely generated.
dim Hom(G_{ℚ_p}, 𝔽_p) = 2 for p odd (unramified and cyclotomic directions).
The proof never uses topological finite generation of G_{F,S}.

nodes.title: The universal lifting ring
nodes.statement: If G satisfies Φ_p then Lift_ρ̄ is pro-represented by a complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebra R^□_ρ̄ ∈ C_𝒪 with a universal lift ρ^□ : G → GL_n(R^□_ρ̄): for every A ∈ C_𝒪, Hom_{C_𝒪}(R^□_ρ̄, A) ≅ Lift_ρ̄(A), f ↦ GL_n(f)∘ρ^□. In particular this holds for G = G_{F,S} and G = G_K.
hypotheses: Uses the framed representability construction of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.2 and the finiteness Φ_p.
proofSteps: Let G′ = ker ρ̄ (open, normal). Every lift sends G′ into Γ̂_n(A), a pro-p group, hence factors through G/H with H the kernel of G′ → G′^{(p)} (maximal pro-p quotient); H is normal in G.
By Φ_p, G′^{(p)} and hence G/H are topologically finitely generated; choose generators γ₁, …, γ_s.

Lift_ρ̄ satisfies Schlessinger's conditions exactly: Lift(A ×_C B) = Lift(A) ×_{Lift(C)} Lift(B) for Artinian fibre products, and its tangent space Z¹(G, ad ρ̄) is finite (tangent-spaces, Φ_p); R03.2 then gives a pro-representing ring.
Concretely R^□_ρ̄ is a quotient of 𝒪[[X^{(i)}_{jk}]], i ≤ s, j, k ≤ n, with ρ^□(γ_i) = [ρ̄(γ_i)] + (X^{(i)}_{jk}), [·] the Teichmüller lift (Kisin's proof).
acceptance: For n = 1, ρ̄ = 1: R^□ = 𝒪[[G^{ab,(p)}]], the completed group algebra of the maximal abelian pro-p quotient.
dim_𝔽 m/(m², λ) = dim Z¹(G, ad ρ̄) (tangent-spaces).
If H²(G, ad ρ̄) = 0 then R^□ is formally smooth of relative dimension dim Z¹(G, ad ρ̄) (Gee Corollary 3.14).

nodes.title: The universal continuous lift over the inverse-limit ring
nodes.statement: ρ^□ : G → GL_n(R^□_ρ̄) = lim_k GL_n(R^□_ρ̄/m^k) is the continuous homomorphism obtained from the compatible universal lifts over the Artinian quotients R^□_ρ̄/m^k; it is continuous for the m-adic topology and, for A ∈ C_𝒪, every continuous lift to GL_n(A) is GL_n(f)∘ρ^□ for a unique f ∈ Hom_{C_𝒪}(R^□_ρ̄, A). The same construction gives ρ^univ over R_ρ̄ (Schur) and the fixed-determinant versions.
hypotheses: R^□_ρ̄ is complete and separated for its maximal-ideal topology (R03.1: objects of C_𝒪 are inverse limits of Artinian quotients).
proofSteps: The pro-representing system (R^□/m^k, ρ_k) is compatible; the limit homomorphism is continuous because each ρ_k is.
For A ∈ C_𝒪 a continuous lift ρ_A gives compatible Artinian lifts ρ_A mod m_A^j, hence compatible maps R^□ → A/m_A^j, hence f : R^□ → A with GL_n(f)∘ρ^□ = ρ_A.
acceptance: For n = 1, ρ̄ = 1: ρ^□ is the tautological character G → G^{ab,(p)} → 𝒪[[G^{ab,(p)}]]^×.
ρ^□ mod m = ρ̄.
Uniqueness: two maps f, f′ with the same composite agree modulo every m_A^j, hence agree.

nodes.title: The universal deformation ring
nodes.statement: If G satisfies Φ_p and ρ̄ is Schur (End_{𝔽[G]}(ρ̄) = 𝔽; e.g. absolutely irreducible), then Def_ρ̄ is pro-represented by R_ρ̄ ∈ C_𝒪 with a universal deformation class [ρ^univ]; without the Schur hypothesis Def_ρ̄ has a hull but need not be pro-representable.
hypotheses: Schlessinger's criterion and the hull/representing-object distinction come from R03.2; R03.2 also warns not to identify a hull with a representing ring when automorphisms obstruct.
proofSteps: Tangent space: Def_ρ̄(𝔽[ε]) = H¹(G, ad ρ̄), finite by Φ_p (tangent-spaces).
H1–H2: Def(A ×_C B) → Def(A) ×_{Def(C)} Def(B) is surjective for C ← B small, and bijective when C = 𝔽: glue lifts after conjugating one of them.

H4: bijectivity for A = B → C small uses that the centraliser of any lift ρ_C in Γ̂_n(C) is Γ̂_n(C) ∩ C^× and lifts: under Schur, Z_{GL_n(A)}(ρ_A) = A^× by induction on length (Gee Lemma 3.7(1) for absolutely irreducible ρ̄).
Alternatively R_ρ̄ is the invariant subring under the free action of the formal group P̂GL_n on Spf R^□_ρ̄ (Kisin's remark), giving framed-unframed-comparison.
acceptance: For ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and H²(G, ad ρ̄) = 0, R_ρ̄ ≅ 𝒪[[x₁, …, x_d]] with d = dim H¹(G, ad ρ̄).
For ρ̄ = 1 ⊕ 1 the centraliser of a lift can be all of Γ̂₂(A), the situation in which R03.2 warns that a hull need not represent; the theorem does not apply.

nodes.title: Framed rings are power series over unframed rings
nodes.statement: If ρ̄ is Schur and G satisfies Φ_p, then R^□_ρ̄ ≅ R_ρ̄[[X_{ij} : 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n]]/(X_{11}), a power series ring in n² − 1 variables, with universal lift ρ^□ = (1_n + X)ρ^univ(1_n + X)^{-1}; the map R_ρ̄ → R^□_ρ̄ is formally smooth of relative dimension n² − 1. The same holds with fixed determinant χ, with the same n² − 1 variables.
hypotheses: Schur ρ̄: the centraliser of a lift in Γ̂_n(A) is the scalars 1 + m_A (strict-vs-full-conjugacy, Carayol for absolutely irreducible ρ̄).
proofSteps: Every lift ρ to A is strictly conjugate to a unique-up-to-scalars lift of the class; given a class [ρ] and a representative, the lifts in the class are aρa^{-1} with a ∈ Γ̂_n(A), and a is determined up to (1 + m_A)·1.
Normalising the (1,1) entry of a − 1 to 0 picks a unique representative of a modulo scalars, so the lifts in a class are parametrised by (m_A)^{n²−1}.
Hence Lift_ρ̄ ≅ Def_ρ̄ × Ĝ_a^{n²−1} functorially, which on representing rings is R^□ ≅ R[[X_{ij}]]/(X_{11}).
Fixed determinant: conjugation preserves the determinant, so the same parametrisation applies to Lift_{ρ̄,χ} → Def_{ρ̄,χ}.
acceptance: n = 1: n² − 1 = 0 and R^□ = R.
Tangent dimensions: dim Z¹ − dim H¹ = n² − dim H⁰ = n² − 1 for Schur ρ̄ (tangent-spaces).
Without Schur (ρ̄ = 1 ⊕ 1) no such comparison exists because Def_ρ̄ is not representable.

nodes.title: Carayol's theorem: absolutely irreducible deformations are determined by traces
nodes.statement: Suppose ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible and let R ∈ C_𝒪 and ρ : G → GL_n(R) a lift. (1) If a ∈ GL_n(R) and aρa^{-1} = ρ then a ∈ R^×. (2) If ρ′ is another lift with tr ρ′ = tr ρ, then ρ′ = aρa^{-1} for some a ∈ Γ̂_n(R). (3) If S ⊆ R is a closed subring in C_𝒪 with m_S = m_R ∩ S and tr ρ(G) ⊆ S, then ρ is Γ̂_n(R)-conjugate to a lift into GL_n(S). Consequently R_ρ̄ is topologically generated over 𝒪 by the traces of ρ^univ.
hypotheses: Absolute irreducibility gives Burnside: ρ̄(𝔽[G]) = M_n(𝔽).
proofSteps: Reduce to R Artinian and induct on length, with I ⊆ R an ideal killed by m_R and ρ ≡ ρ′ mod I; write ρ = ρ′ + δ with δ(σ) ∈ M_n(I) of trace 0.
Multiplicativity gives δ(σ₁σ₂) = ρ̄(σ₁)δ(σ₂) + δ(σ₁)ρ̄(σ₂); for σ₂ ∈ ker ρ̄ this gives tr(ρ̄(σ₁)δ(σ₂)) = 0 for all σ₁, so δ(σ₂) = 0 by Burnside.
Hence δ is a derivation M_n(𝔽) → M_n(I), which is inner: δ(σ) = ρ̄(σ)U − Uρ̄(σ), and ρ′ = (1 − U)ρ(1 + U).
(1) and (3) are proved in the same inductive way (CHT08 Lemmas 2.1.8, 2.1.10).
acceptance: For n = 1 the statement is trivial.
The subring generated by the traces of ρ^univ is dense in R_ρ̄ (Gee Exercise 3.8).
Fails without absolute irreducibility (Kisin Exercise 3(1)).

sources.locator: Lecture 1, Theorem (1.4.1) and its proof, pp. 3–4

nodes.title: Fixed-determinant rings and change of determinant
nodes.statement: Under Φ_p, Lift_{ρ̄,χ} is pro-represented by R^□_{ρ̄,χ} = R^□_ρ̄/(det ρ^□(g) − χ(g) : g ∈ G), and, for Schur ρ̄, Def_{ρ̄,χ} by R_{ρ̄,χ} = R_ρ̄/(det ρ^univ(g) − χ(g)). If p ∤ n: (i) R^□_ρ̄ ≅ R^□_{ρ̄,χ} ⊗̂_𝒪 Λ, Λ = 𝒪[[G^{ab,(p)}]] the universal deformation ring of the trivial character, via ρ ↦ (ρ ⊗ ψ^{-1}, ψ) with ψ = (χ_A^{-1} det ρ)^{1/n}; (ii) for another lift χ′ of det ρ̄, twisting by (χ′χ^{-1})^{1/n} gives R^□_{ρ̄,χ} ≅ R^□_{ρ̄,χ′} (and R_{ρ̄,χ} ≅ R_{ρ̄,χ′}).
hypotheses: p ∤ n: n-th roots exist and are unique in 1 + m_A (a pro-p group) for A ∈ C_𝒪.
proofSteps: Representability: the fixed-determinant condition is the closed condition det ρ = χ, cut out by the stated ideal.

(i): ψ := (χ^{-1} det ρ)^{1/n} is a continuous character with values in 1 + m_A; ρ ⊗ ψ^{-1} has determinant χ; the inverse map is (ρ₀, ψ) ↦ ρ₀ ⊗ ψ, and ψ is a lift of the trivial character, represented by Λ.
(ii): twisting by the n-th root of χ′χ^{-1} ≡ 1 is a natural bijection Lift_{ρ̄,χ} ≅ Lift_{ρ̄,χ′}, compatible with strict conjugation.
acceptance: For n = 1, R^□_{ρ̄,χ} = 𝒪.
For p | n the decomposition (i) can fail: n-th roots of characters in 1 + m_A need not exist (e.g. p = n = 2, G = ℤ₂).
Tangent space of R^□_{ρ̄,χ} is Z¹(G, ad⁰ρ̄) when p ∤ n.

nodes.title: Representing rings under change of coefficients
nodes.statement: For a finite local homomorphism 𝒪 → 𝒪′ with residue extension 𝔽 ⊆ 𝔽′ and ρ̄′ = ρ̄ ⊗ 𝔽′: R^□_{ρ̄′,𝒪′} ≅ R^□_{ρ̄,𝒪} ⊗̂_𝒪 𝒪′ compatibly with the universal lifts; for Schur ρ̄, R_{ρ̄′,𝒪′} ≅ R_{ρ̄,𝒪} ⊗̂_𝒪 𝒪′; and likewise with fixed determinant.
hypotheses: Completed tensor products over 𝒪 and residue-field extension come from R03.1, which also records when they stay Noetherian and local (here: 𝒪′ finite over 𝒪).
proofSteps: By change-of-coefficients, Lift^{𝒪′}_{ρ̄′}(A′) = {lifts of ρ̄ to A′ as an 𝒪-algebra with residue map 𝔽 → 𝔽′} = Hom_{𝒪, local}(R^□_{ρ̄,𝒪}, A′) = Hom_{𝒪′}(R^□_{ρ̄,𝒪} ⊗̂_𝒪 𝒪′, A′).
The representing object is unique up to unique isomorphism, and the universal lifts correspond.
Schur is preserved (change-of-coefficients), so the unframed statement follows in the same way.
acceptance: 𝒪′ = 𝒪: identity.
Tangent spaces change by ⊗_𝔽 𝔽′: H¹(G, ad ρ̄′) = H¹(G, ad ρ̄) ⊗ 𝔽′.

sources.match: The coefficient setting; the base-change argument is the proof steps.

nodes.title: Local deformation problems
nodes.statement: For a profinite group G_v satisfying Φ_p and ρ̄_v : G_v → GL_n(𝔽), a deformation problem D is a collection of lifts (R, ρ) (R ∈ C_𝒪) containing (𝔽, ρ̄_v), closed under pushforward along morphisms of C_𝒪, detected along injections, closed under the fibre products (R₁ ×_{R₁/I₁ ≅ R₂/I₂} R₂), closed under inverse limits along separated filtrations, and stable under conjugation by Γ̂_n(R).
hypotheses: These are the axioms of Clozel–Harris–Taylor as stated by Gee; the local lifting rings they cut out are those of LocalGaloisDeformationRings (R08.x) in applications.
proofSteps: The axioms are closure conditions on sets of lifts; each is checked for a given local condition by its point criterion.
acceptance: The set of all lifts is a deformation problem (the unrestricted problem).
The minimally ramified, ordinary, Fontaine–Laffaille and Steinberg problems of R08.2–R08.4 are deformation problems.
A condition that is not Γ̂_n-stable (e.g. 'ρ(σ) is upper triangular' for a fixed σ in a non-framed sense) is not a deformation problem.

nodes.statement: (1) A deformation problem D corresponds to a Γ̂_n(R^□)-invariant ideal I(D) ⊆ R^□_{ρ̄_v}: (R, ρ) ∈ D iff R^□ → R factors through R^□/I(D). (2) The annihilator L̃(D) ⊆ Z¹(G_v, ad ρ̄) of I(D) in the cotangent space is the preimage of a subspace L(D) ⊆ H¹(G_v, ad ρ̄). (3) Conversely every Γ̂_n-invariant radical ideal I ≠ 𝔪 defines a deformation problem D(I), and I(D(I)) = I, D(I(D)) = D.
hypotheses: Γ̂_n(R^□) acts on R^□ through the universal property (not a group action in general, as Gee warns).
proofSteps: (1): intersect the kernels of R^□ → R over (R, ρ) ∈ D; the fibre-product and limit axioms show the quotient represents D.
(2): Γ̂_n-invariance of I(D) makes its annihilator in Z¹ stable under coboundaries.
(3): the axioms hold for D(I) because I is radical and invariant.
acceptance: The unrestricted problem has I = 0 and L = H¹.
The fixed-determinant condition corresponds to the ideal generated by det ρ^□ − χ.
L(D) for the unramified condition is H¹_ur(G_v, ad ρ̄) = H¹(G_v/I_v, ad ρ̄^{I_v}).

nodes.title: Global deformation data and T-framed deformations
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, S a finite set of places containing those above p and ∞ where ρ̄ ramifies, G = G_{F,S}, ρ̄ : G → GL_n(𝔽) absolutely irreducible, χ a lift of det ρ̄, D_v a deformation problem for ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} for each v ∈ S, and T ⊆ S. A T-framed deformation of type 𝒮 = (S, {D_v}, χ) to A is a class of tuples (ρ, {α_v}_{v∈T}) with ρ a lift of determinant χ, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} ∈ D_v for v ∈ S, α_v ∈ Γ̂_n(A), modulo (ρ, {α_v}) ∼ (βρβ^{-1}, {βα_v}) for β ∈ Γ̂_n(A).
hypotheses: Absolute irreducibility of ρ̄ (Schur suffices for representability; RS-08 keeps the absolutely irreducible statement).
The framed local lift α_v^{-1}ρ|_{G_{F_v}}α_v is well defined (R04.1/restriction-of-deformations).
proofSteps: The equivalence relation is a group action of Γ̂_n(A); the conditions ρ|_{G_{F_v}} ∈ D_v are Γ̂_n-stable, so the functor is well defined.
acceptance: T = ∅ recovers the unframed deformations of type 𝒮 (R^univ_𝒮).
T = S with all D_v unrestricted gives the framed-at-S ring of KW II §4.1 (their tuples (ρ, (ρ_v), (g_v))).
Dropping χ gives the variable-determinant problem of G8.

nodes.title: The relative tangent space is an adjoint Selmer group
nodes.statement: Hom(𝔪_{R^□T}/(𝔪², 𝔪_{R^loc}, λ), 𝔽) ≅ H¹_{S,T}(G_{F,S}, ad⁰ρ̄), the first cohomology of the Selmer-type complex C^•_{S,T}(ad⁰ρ̄) = cone(C^•(G_{F,S}, ad⁰ρ̄) → C^•_{S,T,loc}) with the local conditions L(D_v) at v ∈ S ∖ T and full local cochains (framed) at v ∈ T; its dimension is #T − Σ_{v|∞} h⁰(G_{F_v}, ad⁰) + Σ_{v∈S∖T}(dim L(D_v) − h⁰(G_{F_v}, ad⁰)) + h¹_{S,T}(ad⁰(1)) − h⁰(G_{F,S}, ad⁰(1)).
hypotheses: p ∤ n and T ⊇ {v | p} for the dimension formula (as in Gee); the complex and its long exact sequence come from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.5 (mapping-fibre construction), the Euler characteristic and duality from R02.4/R02.6.
proofSteps: A relative tangent vector is a T-framed deformation to 𝔽[ε] whose framed local lifts at v ∈ T are trivial, i.e. a class in the cone complex (Gee §3.23; KW II Lemma 4.3 counts it for n = 2).
The long exact sequence 0 → H⁰_{S,T} → H⁰(G, ad) → ⊕_T H⁰(G_v, ad) → H¹_{S,T} → H¹(G, ad⁰) → ⊕_T H¹ ⊕ ⊕_{S∖T} H¹/L(D_v) → H²_{S,T} → … computes it.
Poitou–Tate identifies H³_{S,T} ≅ H⁰(ad⁰(1))^∨ and H²_{S,T} ≅ H¹_{S,T}(ad⁰(1))^∨ (with the dual conditions L(D_v)^⊥); the global and local Euler characteristic formulas give the dimension.
acceptance: n = 2, p > 2, KW II conventions (S containing the infinite places, all framed): g = h¹_{L^⊥}(S, (ad⁰)*(1)) + |S| − 1 (KW II preprint, proof of Proposition 4.4).
T = ∅: the tangent space of R^univ_𝒮 is the Selmer group H¹_{{L(D_v)}}(G_{F,S}, ad⁰ρ̄).
For p = 2 the trace-zero module and its dual are not isomorphic and the δ₂ corrections of KW II Lemma 4.2 appear.

nodes.title: Presentation of the global ring over the local rings
nodes.statement: R^□T_𝒮 ≅ R^loc_{S,T}[[x₁, …, x_g]]/J with g = h¹_{S,T}(G_{F,S}, ad⁰ρ̄), inducing an isomorphism on relative tangent spaces, and the minimal number of generators r(J) = dim J/𝔪J satisfies r(J) ≤ h²_{S,T}(ad⁰ρ̄) = h¹_{S,T}(G_{F,S}, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) (the dual Selmer group with conditions L(D_v)^⊥).
hypotheses: The obstruction pairing uses Poitou–Tate duality and the product formula for local invariants (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4); the relation-count algebra is DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.2.
RS-08 cites the KW II form of this bound through Proposition 4.5 (published numbering), whose proof contains it as Lemma 4.6; the ESI preprint numbers it Lemma 4.5 (n = 2, T = S).
proofSteps: Choose g elements lifting a basis of the relative cotangent space: R^loc[[x]] ↠ R^□T by relative Nakayama (relative-tangent-space).
For u ∈ Hom(J/𝔪J, 𝔽), push out 0 → J/𝔪J → R^loc[[x]]/𝔪J → R^□T → 0 along u; the obstruction to lifting the universal object gives a 2-cocycle c with c|_{G_v} = ∂a_v.
Pair with x ∈ H¹_{L^⊥}(S, ad⁰(1)) by Σ_v inv(x_v ∪ a_v + z_v), where ∂z = x ∪ c; this is independent of choices by the product formula, and u ↦ (x ↦ (x, u)) is injective (KW II preprint Lemma 4.5).
Hence r(J) ≤ h¹_{L^⊥}(S, ad⁰(1)) = h²_{S,T}(ad⁰).
acceptance: g − r(J) ≥ #T − Σ_{v|∞} h⁰(G_{F_v}, ad⁰) + Σ_{v∈S∖T}(dim L(D_v) − h⁰(G_{F_v}, ad⁰)) − h⁰(G_{F,S}, ad⁰(1)) (from relative-tangent-space; Gee takes S and T to consist of finite places).
n = 2, p > 2, KW II conventions (their S contains the infinite places, and every place of S is framed): g − r ≥ |S| − 1 (KW II preprint, proof of Proposition 4.4).
When H¹_{S,T}(ad⁰(1)) = 0 the global ring is a power-series ring over R^loc.

nodes.title: Lower bound for the dimension of global deformation rings
nodes.statement: Krull dim R^univ_𝒮 ≥ 1 + Σ_{v∈S}(Krull dim(R^□_{ρ̄|G_v,χ}/I(D_v)) − n²) − Σ_{v|∞} h⁰(G_{F_v}, ad⁰ρ̄) − h⁰(G_{F,S}, ad⁰ρ̄(1)). In the setting of KW II (n = 2, F totally real, ρ̄ odd, fixed determinant, framed local rings of relative dimension 3 at finite places not above p, 3 + [F_v : ℚ_p] above p and 2 at infinite places), the absolute dimension of R̄^ψ_S is ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Restriction to a finite extension as a ring map
nodes.statement: Let F′/F be a finite extension and S′ the places of F′ above S. Restricting lifts along G_{F′,S′} → G_{F,S} gives a local 𝒪-algebra map res : R^□_{ρ̄|G_{F′,S′}} → R^□_{ρ̄} of framed rings and, with fixed determinant, R^□_{ρ̄|,χ|G_{F′}} → R^□_{ρ̄,χ}. If ρ̄|G_{F′,S′} is absolutely irreducible it gives res : R^univ_{ρ̄|G_{F′,S′}} → R^univ_{ρ̄} on unframed rings. If for each v′ | v the local problem D_{v′} contains the restrictions to G_{F′_{v′}} of the lifts in D_v, res descends to the rings with local conditions, R̄_{F′} → R̄_F (KW II's γ).
hypotheses: Absolute irreducibility of ρ̄|G_{F′,S′} is what makes the unframed ring of the restriction exist (R04.2/universal-deformation-ring); the framed map needs no hypothesis.
The compatibility of local problems is checked in each application; KW II choose F′ so that it holds (proof of Theorem 10.1).
proofSteps: G_{F′} → G_F → G_{F,S} factors through G_{F′,S′}, since a place of F′ not above S is unramified in F′F_S/F′.
Restriction of lifts and of strict classes is natural in A (R04.1/restriction-of-deformations); the Yoneda lemma gives the ring map, and det(ρ|G_{F′}) = (det ρ)|G_{F′}.
Under the compatibility hypothesis the restriction of the universal lift over R̄_F lies in D_{v′} at every v′, so res factors through R̄_{F′}.
acceptance: F′ = F gives the identity, and for F ⊆ F′ ⊆ F″ the maps compose.
res is in general neither injective, surjective nor flat (restriction-finiteness gives a finite, non-flat example).

nodes.title: Finiteness of restriction maps
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a profinite group satisfying Φ_p, Σ ⊆ Γ an open subgroup and ρ̄ : Γ → GL_n(𝔽) with ρ̄|Σ absolutely irreducible. Then the restriction map R^univ_{ρ̄|Σ} → R^univ_{ρ̄} makes R^univ_{ρ̄} a finitely generated R^univ_{ρ̄|Σ}-module. In particular, for F′/F finite with ρ̄|G_{F′,S′} absolutely irreducible, R^univ_{ρ̄} is finite over R^univ_{ρ̄|G_{F′,S′}} (Khare–Wintenberger). Nothing is claimed about flatness or injectivity: finite flatness of a restriction map is a separate theorem when it holds.
hypotheses: BLGGT prove this for 𝒢_n-valued representations (and for twists and for I(r)); Gee states the GL_n case. The proof below is BLGGT's specialised to GL_n, with Carayol's theorem (R04.2/carayol-trace-theorem) in place of CHT08 Lemma 2.1.12.
Absolute irreducibility of ρ̄|Σ is used twice: for R^univ_{ρ̄|Σ} to exist, and (through ρ̄) so that traces generate R^univ_{ρ̄}.
proofSteps: Write R = R^univ_{ρ̄}, R_Σ = R^univ_{ρ̄|Σ} and 𝔪 = 𝔪_{R_Σ}. The image of Γ in GL_n(R/𝔪R) is finite: modulo 𝔪, ρ^univ|Σ is conjugate to ρ̄|Σ, so the kernel contains ker(ρ̄|Σ), which is open in Γ.

Let m be the order of that image, γ₁, …, γ_m representatives, and f(T) = ∏_{(ζ₁,…,ζ_n)∈μ_m(𝔽̄)^n}(T − (ζ₁ + ⋯ + ζ_n)) ∈ 𝔽[T]. In the universal algebra 𝔽[X_{ij}]/(X^m = 1) all eigenvalues of X are m-th roots of unity, so f(tr X) lies in every prime and f(tr X)^a = 0 for some a.

Hence T_i ↦ tr ρ^univ(γ_i) defines 𝔽[T₁, …, T_m]/(f(T_i)^a) → R/𝔪R. R is topologically generated over 𝒪 by the traces (Carayol), and tr ρ^univ(γ) ≡ tr ρ^univ(γ_i) mod 𝔪R when γ and γ_i have the same image, so the map has dense image; its source is finite, so it is surjective and R/𝔪R is finite over 𝔽.
R is 𝔪_R-adically complete and separated and 𝔪R ⊆ 𝔪_R, so the complete Nakayama lemma makes R finite over R_Σ.
acceptance: Finite but not flat: p odd, Γ = ℤ_p ⋊ {±1} (−1 acting by inversion), Σ = ℤ_p, n = 1, ρ̄ = 1. Commutators are the elements a^{−2}, so Γ^{ab,(p)} = 1 while Σ^{ab,(p)} = ℤ_p; the map is R_Σ = 𝒪⟦Y⟧ → R = 𝒪, Y ↦ 0, finite and not flat.
The same example shows finiteness does not pass from R to R_Σ: R = 𝒪 is finite over 𝒪 but 𝒪⟦Y⟧ is not.
Σ = Γ gives the identity.

Consequence used by PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.1 (KW II Theorem 10.1): if the local conditions are compatible under restriction and R̄_{F′} is finite over 𝒪, then R̄_F, a quotient of R^univ_F and so finite over R̄_{F′}, is finite over 𝒪. The implication runs one way only (first example).

nodes.title: Enlarging the ramification set gives closed immersions
nodes.statement: Let S ⊆ S′ be finite sets of places of F containing the places above p and ∞, with ρ̄ unramified outside S. Inflation along G_{F,S′} ↠ G_{F,S} identifies lifts unramified outside S with lifts over G_{F,S′} that are trivial on the inertia groups at the places of S′ ∖ S. The induced maps R^□_{S′} → R^□_S, R_{S′} → R_S (ρ̄ absolutely irreducible) and their fixed-determinant versions are surjective, with kernel the ideal generated by the entries of ρ^univ(σ) − 1 for σ in the inertia groups at places above S′ ∖ S. The same holds with local conditions when the condition at v ∈ S′ ∖ S is 'unramified'.
hypotheses: A map B → C of complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras is surjective (a closed immersion) exactly when Sp_C(A) → Sp_B(A) is injective for all A, and it suffices to test A = 𝔽[ε] (KW II §2.1).
proofSteps: ker(G_{F,S′} → G_{F,S}) is the closed normal subgroup generated by the inertia groups at places above S′ ∖ S, so the two functors of lifts agree.
The subfunctor inclusion is injective on 𝔽[ε]-points, so the cotangent map is surjective and the ring map is surjective by complete Nakayama.

The quotient by the stated ideal classifies exactly the lifts trivial on those inertia groups: conjugate inertia elements give entries in the same ideal, and ideals of a Noetherian complete local ring are closed.
For unframed rings the ideal is independent of the representative in the strict class, since conjugation preserves it.
acceptance: S′ = S gives the identity.
KW II Proposition 5.11: for Taylor–Wiles places Q, R̄^ψ_{S∪Q} modulo the augmentation ideal of 𝒪[Δ′_Q] is R̄^ψ_S.
The map is not injective in general: its tangent map is H¹(G_{F,S}, ad) ↪ H¹(G_{F,S′}, ad), usually a strict inclusion.

nodes.title: Twisting isomorphisms and change of determinant
nodes.statement: Let μ : G_{F,S} → 𝒪^× be a continuous character. Twisting ρ ↦ μ ⊗ ρ gives isomorphisms R^□_{ρ̄} ≅ R^□_{μ̄⊗ρ̄} and, when they exist, R^univ_{ρ̄} ≅ R^univ_{μ̄⊗ρ̄}, carrying the determinant-χ quotients to the determinant-μ^nχ quotients and each local problem D_v to μ|G_v ⊗ D_v. If χ′χ^{−1} = μ^n with μ residually trivial then R_{ρ̄,χ} ≅ R_{ρ̄,χ′}. For n = 2 and p > 2 every residually trivial ν is μ² with μ residually trivial, so the determinant can be changed freely within its residual class; for p = 2 it cannot, and KW II change it only after a solvable totally real base change split at prescribed places (Lemma 7.10, via Grunwald–Wang).
hypotheses: For p ∤ n the decomposition R^□ ≅ R^□_χ ⊗̂ 𝒪⟦G^{ab,(p)}⟧ is R04.2/fixed-determinant-rings; this node supplies the maps between different χ and the twists of local problems.

KW II Lemma 7.10 is a statement about Hecke characters; it is not planned here and stays with its consumer (GL2ModularityLifting). Its Grunwald–Wang input is outside the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap and is planned under InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.4.
proofSteps: μ ⊗ − is a bijection on lifts, natural in A, with inverse μ^{−1} ⊗ −, and it commutes with strict conjugation; Yoneda gives the ring isomorphisms.
det(μ ⊗ ρ) = μ^n det ρ, and local problems are transported by the same bijection at each v.
For p odd, 1 + π𝒪 is a pro-p abelian group on which squaring is bijective, so ν^{1/2} is a continuous residually trivial character.
acceptance: μ = 1 gives the identity, and (μμ′) ⊗ − = μ ⊗ (μ′ ⊗ −).

p = 2, F = ℚ: the character ν of Gal(ℚ(i)/ℚ) is residually trivial (−1 ≡ 1 mod 2), but ν = μ² would make μ of order 4 with ℚ(i) inside the cyclic quartic field it cuts out, and ℚ(i) lies in no cyclic quartic extension of ℚ (−1 is not a sum of two squares). So twisting cannot move the determinant χ to χν.
Twisting by μ changes the ring only by relabelling: tr(μ ⊗ ρ) = μ · tr ρ.

nodes.title: Diagonalizable groups on complete local algebras
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated abelian group a whose torsion has p-power order, the diagonalizable group (a)* on complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras is the completion of the diagonalizable group scheme D(a) at the identity of its special fibre: (a)*(A) = Hom(a, 1 + 𝔪_A), with affine algebra the completion of 𝒪[a] at (π, augmentation ideal). T = (ℤ^t)* = Ĝ_m^t is the split formal torus and T_{p^m} = ((ℤ/p^m)^t)* = μ_{p^m}^t. Truncation: the closed immersion T_{p^m} ↪ T is an isomorphism after truncation at level m + 1 (A ↦ A/𝔪^{m+1}), because (1 + X)^{p^m} − 1 ∈ (p, X)^{m+1}.
hypotheses: KW II use these for the twisting groups G*_V (V a set of auxiliary places) and for the torus T of 2-adic patching.
proofSteps: (a)*(A) = Hom(a, 1 + 𝔪_A): points of D(a) are homomorphisms a → A^×, and completing at the identity of the special fibre keeps those reducing to 1.
Truncation: the coefficient of X^k in (1 + X)^{p^m} − 1 has p-adic valuation m − v_p(k), and k − v_p(k) ≥ 1, so each term lies in (p, X)^{m+1}.
acceptance: a = ℤ: (a)*(A) = 1 + 𝔪_A, with affine algebra 𝒪⟦X⟧.
a = ℤ/p^m: (a)*(A) = μ_{p^m}(A), since p^m-th roots of 1 in a local ring with residue field of characteristic p reduce to 1.

nodes.title: Quotients by free actions
nodes.statement: Let G be a group functor on complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras represented by a formally smooth algebra, acting freely on X = Sp A(X): the map G × X → X × X, (g, x) ↦ (x, gx), is a closed immersion, equivalently G(A) acts without fixed points on X(A) for every A. Then the orbit functor O is represented by the invariant algebra A(X)⁰ = {a : γ(a) = 1 ⊗ a}, X → O is smooth, t_O = t_X/t_G, and X ≅ O × G as a trivial G-torsor over O; so dim A(X) = dim A(X)⁰ + dim G. If instead D = (a)* is diagonalizable (possibly finite) and acts freely, the quotient D\X exists with affine algebra A(X)⁰, X is a D-torsor over it, and for a ↠ a′ the quotient can be taken in stages.
hypotheses: Schlessinger's criterion is imported from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.2.

For finite diagonalizable D, KW II cite SGA 3, Exp. VIII, Theorem 5.1 (quotients by finite diagonalizable groups); the affine free-action quotient is requested from Tau Ceti ModularCurves 0C. KW II call the general diagonalizable case 'dévissage de routine'; the planned proof filters a by its torsion subgroup and uses the quotient in stages.
proofSteps: Schlessinger (H1), surjectivity: lift g_A ∈ G(A) along B₁ ↠ A using smoothness of G, then glue.
(H1), injectivity: two elements of X(B₁ ×_A B₂) with the same image differ by g_i ∈ G(B_i) whose images in G(A) agree by freeness, so they differ by an element of G(B₁ ×_A B₂).
(H2): t_X → t_O is surjective and linear, so t_O is finite-dimensional; freeness makes t_G → t_X injective and t_O = t_X/t_G.
Smoothness of X → O: lift the element of G(A) relating two points, again by smoothness of G. A section s of the smooth map gives X ≅ G × O, x ↦ (g, x̄) with x = g·s(x̄).
Functions on G × O constant on G-orbits are exactly A(O), so A(O) = A(X)⁰.
acceptance: G trivial: A(X)⁰ = A(X).
Ĝ_m acting on Sp 𝒪⟦x, y⟧ by λ·(x, y) = (λ(1 + x) − 1, y) is free, with invariant ring 𝒪⟦y⟧ and quotient map smooth of relative dimension 1.
Ĝ_m acting trivially on Sp 𝒪 is not free, and Sp 𝒪 ≇ O × Ĝ_m: freeness is needed.
With G = Ĝ_m^γ this gives the smoothness of relative dimension γ used by Newton–Thorne (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B item 60).

nodes.title: Free actions assembled from truncated actions
nodes.statement: For m ≥ 1 let C^{[m]} be the complete local 𝒪-algebras with 𝔪^m = 0, and define group chunks and group-action chunks of level m by truncating the group-scheme axioms, products being truncated ((A₁ ⊗ A₂)^{[m]}). Let C be a complete local 𝒪-algebra with compatible surjections C ↠ A_m (A_m ∈ C^{[m]}), A_∞ = lim A_m, and G a representable group with compatible action chunks of G^{[m]} on Sp A_m. Then there is a unique action of G on Sp A_∞ compatible with the chunks, and it is free if the chunks are. With the truncation isomorphism of diagonalizable-groups, free actions of the finite groups T_{p^n} give free action chunks of the torus T, and hence free T-actions on patched limits.
hypotheses: This is the device by which KW II obtain the free Ĝ_m^t-action on the 2-adic patched ring from the twisting actions of the finite groups G*_{Q_n} (proof of Proposition 9.3).
proofSteps: For each m some n has Sp(A_∞)^{[m]} ↪ Sp A_n, so the given chunks restrict to the truncations of Sp A_∞.
The immersions G^{[m]} × X^{[m]}_∞ → (G^{[2m]} × X^{[2m]}_∞)^{[2m]} define the action map G × X_∞ → X_∞ in the limit; uniqueness is by the truncations.
A map is a closed immersion if and only if all its truncations are, so freeness of the chunks gives freeness of the limit action.
acceptance: Constant systems A_m = A^{[m]} recover an action of G on Sp A.
A(Y) → A(X) is surjective if and only if A(Y)^{[m]} → A(X)^{[m]} is surjective for some m ≥ 2.
A₁ ⊗_𝒪 A₂ need not lie in C^{[m]} when A₁, A₂ do, which is why chunks use the truncated product.

nodes.title: The action of twisting characters
nodes.statement: Let W = S ∪ V with S ∩ V = ∅, S containing the places above p and ∞ (KW II §4.1). Let G_V = Gal(F^S_V/F), the Galois group of the maximal abelian p-extension of F unramified outside V and split at S; it is a finite abelian p-group. The diagonalizable group G*_V (G*_V(A) = residually trivial Hom(G_V, A^×)) acts on Sp R^□_{S∪V} (determinant fixed only on S) by χ·(ρ, (ρ_v), (g_v)) = (χ ⊗ ρ, (ρ_v), (g_v)); each χ ∈ G*_V(𝒪) gives an automorphism a_χ with a_χ ∘ ρ^univ = χ ⊗ ρ^univ, commuting with the ∏_{v∈S}(GL_2)_1 action on frames. For p = 2 the subgroup G*_{V,2} of characters of G_V/2G_V preserves the determinant and acts on Sp R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V}. The actions descend to the quotients with local conditions at S and to the unframed (trace) subrings.
hypotheses: Finiteness of G_V is class field theory: G_V is the p-part of a ray class group of modulus supported on V (tame, as V has no place above p) modulo the classes of places in S; requested from Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory.
For n = 2 as in KW II; for general n the determinant changes by χ^n.
proofSteps: χ ⊗ ρ is unramified outside W; for v ∈ S, χ|D_v = 1 because χ is split at v, so (χ ⊗ ρ)|D_v = ρ|D_v, the framed local data (ρ_v, g_v) are unchanged and det(χ ⊗ ρ)|D_v = ψχ_p.
The twist is natural in A, which gives the action of the group functor G*_V, and Yoneda gives a_χ for χ with values in 𝒪^×.
The frame action changes only (ρ_v, g_v), so the two actions commute.
For χ ∈ G*_{V,2}(A), χ² = 1, so det(χ ⊗ ρ) = χ² det ρ = det ρ.
Local conditions at S are untouched, and a_χ(tr ρ^univ(g)) = χ(g) tr ρ^univ(g) with χ(g) ∈ 𝒪, so the trace subrings are preserved.
acceptance: χ = 1 acts trivially and a_χ a_{χ′} = a_{χχ′}.
For p odd G*_{V,2} is trivial (χ² = 1 with χ of p-power order forces χ = 1), so twisting gives no action on fixed-determinant rings.
KW II Lemma 5.12: on R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n}, a_χ ∘ δ = χ(δ)(δ ∘ a_χ) for δ ∈ Δ′_{Q_n}, since a_χ(γ_v(δ)) = χ(δ)γ_v(δ) (the compatibility with R04.5's diamond action).

nodes.title: Freeness of dyadic twisting and its stabilisers
nodes.statement: Let p = 2 and suppose ρ̄ : G_F → GL_2(𝔽) has non-solvable image. For every A and every non-trivial χ ∈ Hom(G_V, A^×) residually trivial, no lift ρ_A is equivalent to χ ⊗ ρ_A. Hence the actions of G*_V on Sp R^□_{S∪V}, of G*_{V,2} on Sp R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V}, and on their unframed and local-condition quotients, are free: every stabiliser is trivial. Without the image hypothesis stabilisers can be non-trivial.
hypotheses: KW II deduce the image fact from Dickson's theorem (projective image SL_2(𝔽_{2^r}), r > 1); step 1 below uses only non-solvability.
proofSteps: Let H = ker χ, so G_F/H is an abelian 2-group. ρ̄|H is absolutely irreducible: over 𝔽̄, if H fixed a unique line then G_F would fix it and ρ̄ would land in a Borel (solvable); if exactly two lines, G_F would permute them and the projective image would be an extension of a subgroup of ℤ/2 by a torus (solvable); if all lines, H would act by scalars and the projective image would be a quotient of G_F/H (abelian).
By Burnside the 𝔽-span of ρ̄(H) is M_2(𝔽). The trace form is non-degenerate, so for g₀ with χ(g₀) ≠ 1 there is h ∈ H with tr ρ̄(g₀h) ≠ 0; put g = g₀h, so χ(g) = χ(g₀) ≠ 1.
tr(χ ⊗ ρ_A)(g) − tr ρ_A(g) = (χ(g) − 1) tr ρ_A(g) ≠ 0 because tr ρ_A(g) is a unit, while equivalent lifts have equal traces.
Freeness in the sense of free-action-quotient is the absence of fixed points on A-points, which is what was shown.
acceptance: Dihedral stabiliser (p = 2): if ρ = Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} θ with K/F quadratic, unramified outside V and split at S, and ε = ε_{K/F} (values ±1, residually trivial), then ε ⊗ ρ = MρM^{−1} with M = diag(1, −1) ≡ 1 mod 2 in the induced basis, so ρ is fixed by ε and the action is not free; here ρ̄ = Ind θ̄ has solvable image.
For p odd the same trace argument applies whenever ρ̄|ker χ is absolutely irreducible.
Freeness is what makes the twisted quotients representable (free-action-quotient) and gives the torsor of determinant-twist-torsor.

nodes.title: Rings with determinant fixed only on S, and the determinant map
nodes.statement: (KW II §4.1.1, n = 2.) R^□_{S∪V} represents tuples (V_A, (β_{v,A})_{v∈S}) with V_A a deformation of ρ̄ as a G_{F,S∪V}-representation such that det V_A|D_v = ψχ_p for v ∈ S, and β_{v,A} lifts of the chosen basis; R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} is the same with det V_A = ψχ_p globally. Both are R^{□,loc,ψ}_S-algebras, and R̄ denotes base change to the local-condition quotient R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S. The determinant map d : Sp R^□_{S∪V} → G*_V, ρ ↦ det ρ · (ψχ_p)^{−1}, satisfies d(χ ⊗ ρ) = χ² d(ρ), and Sp R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} = d^{−1}(1) is a closed subfunctor.
hypotheses: These are Newton–Thorne's R′_Q and R′^□_Q for p = 2 with V = Q a set of Taylor–Wiles places (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B item 7).
The unframed variants are the trace subrings; the framed rings are power series in 4|S| − 1 variables over them (KW II Proposition 4.1, R04.2/framed-unframed-comparison).
proofSteps: det ρ · (ψχ_p)^{−1} is residually trivial, unramified outside S ∪ V and trivial on D_v for v ∈ S, so it is split at S and unramified outside V; its values lie in the pro-p group 1 + 𝔪_A, so it factors through G_V.
det(χ ⊗ ρ) = χ² det ρ for 2 × 2 matrices.
d^{−1}(1) is cut out by the ideal generated by d^*(g) − 1, g ∈ G_V.
acceptance: If G_V = 1 then R^□_{S∪V} = R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V}.
For p odd squaring is bijective on G*_V(A), so ρ ↦ (d(ρ)^{−1/2} ⊗ ρ, d(ρ)^{1/2}) gives Sp R^□_{S∪V} ≅ Sp R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} × G*_V.

For p = 2, (x, χ) ↦ χ ⊗ x from Sp R^{□,ψ} × G*_V to Sp R^□ is not injective when G_V ≠ 1 (G*_V[2] acts on both factors) and misses the points where d is not a square; this is why KW II pass through the invariant ring (determinant-twist-torsor).

nodes.title: The determinant torsor for dyadic twisting
nodes.statement: Let T = Ĝ_m^γ act freely on X′ = Sp R′ with invariant ring R^inv (free-action-quotient), and let d : X′ → T satisfy d(λx) = λ² d(x). Put X = d^{−1}(1) = Sp R. Then X′ → Sp R^inv is smooth of relative dimension γ, T₂ = T[2] acts freely on X, and X → Sp R^inv is a T₂-torsor; hence R is finite flat of degree 2^γ over R^inv and dim R = dim R^inv = dim R′ − γ.
hypotheses: KW II prove this for the 2-adic patched rings (Lemma 9.4, with T the torus through which the twisting groups G*_{Q_n} are patched); Newton–Thorne state it for R′_∞ (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B item 60). The statement here is the abstract form of KW II's proof.
T must be a torus: squaring T → T is finite flat with kernel T₂ (1 + X ↦ (1 + X)² is 2X + X², a distinguished polynomial of degree 2), which fails for finite diagonalizable groups.
proofSteps: Form X′ ×_T T = {(x, λ) : d(x) = λ²}. T acts diagonally, λ′·(x, λ) = (λ′x, λ′λ), which preserves it since d(λ′x) = λ′²λ²; T₂ acts by translation on λ. It is a torsor over Sp R^inv under T × T₂.
(x, λ) ↦ (λ^{−1}x, λ) is an isomorphism X′ ×_T T ≅ X × T, with inverse (y, λ) ↦ (λy, λ). Under it T acts trivially on X and by translation on T, and η ∈ T₂ acts by (y, λ) ↦ (ηy, ηλ).
Taking the quotient by T first (free-action-quotient) leaves X with a free T₂-action whose quotient is Sp R^inv (quotients in stages).
Smoothness of relative dimension γ of X′ → Sp R^inv is free-action-quotient with G = T, and a finite flat torsor preserves Krull dimension.
acceptance: γ = 0: T is trivial and R = R′ = R^inv.
If d(λx) = λ d(x) instead, then x ↦ (d(x)^{−1}x, d(x)) gives X′ ≅ X × T and X → Sp R^inv is an isomorphism, not a T₂-torsor: the squaring is what produces T₂.
KW II Lemma 9.5 uses dim R = dim R^inv = dim R′ − γ to show that R′_∞ is a power series ring.

nodes.title: Inertia-rigid deformation rings
nodes.statement: Let G be profinite with a finite normal subgroup I and G/I ≅ ℤ̂, F ∈ G mapping to a generator, ρ̄ : G → GL_d(𝔽) and ρ₀ : G → GL_d(𝒪) a lift with determinant φ. Let M_{φ,0} be the affine 𝒪-scheme of DATA (ρ_I : I → GL_d, f ∈ GL_d with int(f)ρ_I = ρ_I ∘ int(F), det ρ_I = φ|I, det f = φ(F)) whose characteristic polynomials ρ_I(τ) equal those of ρ₀(τ) for τ ∈ I, and R^□_{φ,0,fl} the completion at the point ξ_{ρ̄} of its p-torsion-free quotient. Then ξ_{ρ̄} lies on the flat part, every irreducible component of Spec R^□_{φ,0,fl} is faithfully flat over 𝒪 of absolute dimension d², R^□_{φ,0,fl}[1/p] is regular, and its 𝒪′-points are exactly the lifts with determinant φ whose restriction to I is conjugate over E′ to ρ₀|I. So it is the quotient of R^□ classifying these lifts.
hypotheses: Applied (KW II §3.3) to G = G_{F_v}/ker(ρ₀|I_{F_v}) for v ∤ p, whose inertia image is finite once ρ₀ is fixed. LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2 plans fixed-inertial-type quotients in general; this node is KW II's explicit model for finite inertial image, which RS-08 places here.

Excellence of finite-type 𝒪-algebras, regularity of completion maps and equidimensionality (KW II cite Matsumura, Commutative Algebra §34 and Theorem 79, and Commutative Ring Theory Theorem 31.6) are requested from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3.
proofSteps: M_{φ,0} → GL_d^{|I|+1} is a closed immersion cut out by the multiplication table of I, the action of int(F) and the determinant; ρ₀ gives an 𝒪-point specialising to ξ_{ρ̄}, so ξ_{ρ̄} lies on the flat part (Lemma 2.9).
Forgetting f maps M_{φ,0}[1/p] to M_I ≅ GL_d/C* (conjugates of ρ₀|I, C the commutant) and makes it a torsor under C*₁ (determinant 1), so it is smooth of dimension d² − dim C* + dim C*₁ = d² − 1.

Finite-type 𝒪-algebras are excellent, so the completion map is regular and R^□_{φ,0,fl}[1/p] is regular; faithful flatness gives each component of the localisation dimension d², and R^□_{φ,0,fl} is equidimensional.
Representations of the finite group I over E′ are determined by their characters, so equal characteristic polynomials mean ρ|I ⊗ E′ ≅ ρ₀|I ⊗ E′ (Proposition 2.11).
acceptance: d = 1: ρ_I = φ|I and f = φ(F) are forced, so M_{φ,0} = Spec 𝒪 and R^□_{φ,0,fl} = 𝒪, of absolute dimension 1 = d².
I = 1 (unramified lifts with fixed determinant): M_{φ,0} = {f ∈ GL_d : det f = φ(F)} and R^□_{φ,0,fl} ≅ 𝒪⟦x₁, …, x_{d²−1}⟧.
R^□_{φ,0,fl} is characterised by its 𝒪′-points (KW II Corollary 2.3), not as a functor on Artinian rings.

sourceIssues.printed: The source defines condition Φp for G by requiring the maximal pro-p quotient of each finite index subgroup G′ ⊂ G to have finitely many topological generators. It claims equivalence with finite dimensionality of Hom(G, Fp).
sourceIssues.correction: “This is equivalent to asking that Hom(G′, 𝔽_p) is finite dimensional for every open G′ ⊂ G” (as the same notes' Exercise 1 states).
sourceIssues.reason: Finiteness of Hom(G, 𝔽_p) for G alone is strictly weaker: for p odd, G = (∏_ℕ ℤ/p) ⋊ ℤ/2 with ℤ/2 acting by inversion has abelianisation ℤ/2 (the commutators a^{-2} fill ∏ ℤ/p since 2 is invertible), so Hom(G, 𝔽_p) = 0, while its open subgroup ∏_ℕ ℤ/p of index 2 has infinite Hom to 𝔽_p and is not topologically finitely generated. Exercise 1 on p. 4 of the same notes states the correct equivalence with all open subgroups.

sourceIssues.printed: The source says the converse follows readily from SpC(A) → SpB(A) being surjective when A = F[ϵ], citing [45].
sourceIssues.correction: “… using the injectivity of Sp_C(A) → Sp_B(A) for A = 𝔽[ε]”: injectivity on tangent spaces makes the cotangent map surjective, and complete Nakayama then makes B → C surjective.
sourceIssues.reason: The converse assumes that Sp_C(A) → Sp_B(A) is injective for all A; surjectivity of this map is neither given nor true for a proper closed immersion (for B = 𝒪⟦x⟧ → C = 𝒪, the tangent map t_C = 0 → t_B = 𝔽 is not surjective). The argument that works uses injectivity at A = 𝔽[ε].
